_: Text that LOOKS like plain-text maths and is not: a slash between two whole numbers that is not a fraction, or a letter and a digit that are not a lost power. Kept as written on purpose. Read by tools/typeset-plain-maths.py (which leaves these alone) and by js/check-typeset.js (which accepts these and fails on any other). One reason each, keyed by row and by the exact text. A new row is not on this list, so it fails until somebody decides which it is.

Q-AQA-7408-2306-3A-016.41/42: n = 41/42 means n is 41 or 42 -- two alternatives in the mark scheme, not forty-one forty-seconds

Q-AQA-8464B-2406-2H-033.50/50: fifty-fifty, a ratio said aloud -- and the sentence is about the scheme NOT accepting it written that way

Q-AQA-7408-1706-3BA-036.0/3: a mark score, nought out of three, not a fraction anybody works with

Q-AQA-7408-2406-1-24.60 / 540: the working as it is keyed into a calculator, 42 000 x 60 / 540, a chain of operations rather than one fraction

Q-AQA-7408-2406-1-27.12 / 16: the same: 2.0 x 12 / 16, keyed as a chain

Q-AQA-7408-2306-3A-014.3 / 2: truncated to 3 / 2 sf means three or two significant figures

Q-STA-KS2-2024-P3-19.r1: remainder 1 in a bus-stop division, which is how KS2 writes a remainder -- not r to the power 1
